toolParallelBiohCoverTotals

Source: R/toolParallelBiohCoverTotals.R
toolParallelBiohCoverTotals.Rd

For the absoluteChanges harmonizer, keep the bioh cover totals (forest: bioh.primf/secmf/secyf/pltns, other: bioh.primn/secnf) parallel to the input (constant offset) after the harmonization year.

Usage

toolParallelBiohCoverTotals(xInput, xTarget, biohCalculated, harmonizationYear)

Arguments

xInput

recategorized input nonland data, containing the harmonization year and the years after it

xTarget

extrapolated target nonland data, providing the anchor in the harmonization year, its years up to the harmonization year are returned unchanged

biohCalculated

recalculated bioh (harmonized kg C per Mha times harmonized harvest area), providing the allocation weight, only its years after the harmonization year are used

harmonizationYear

integer year the input changes are measured from

Value

bioh for all years: the target data up to the harmonization year, then the allocated cover targets for the years after it; the tool checks its own allocation for regional and global parallelism of every cover to the balanced targets

Details

toolParallelCoverTargets computes the regional cover targets (absolute amounts per region and year). toolAllocateRegionTotals distributes each regional target over the clusters of the region, proportional to their recalculated bioh. Within a cluster, the amount is split over the cover's bioh items, proportional to their recalculated bioh. Clusters with zero recalculated bioh get nothing.

Processing steps, per year after the harmonization year:

  • Regional cover target: the value from the target data in the harmonization year plus the change in the input since that year.

  • Set negative regional targets to zero. This raises their sum. To compensate, scale the regional targets > 0 down, so the global cover total equals the raw global target. Regions set to zero get nothing.

  • Set a negative global cover target to zero. The clipped loss is compensated for by the other cover: its regional targets are scaled by one common factor, so the global total over both covers stays input parallel. The scaled targets are the balanced targets, the resulting global total the balanced global target.

  • Distribute each cover's balanced regional target over the clusters of the region, proportional to their recalculated bioh (regional weight: summed recalculated bioh of the cover's items), and split the amount of each cluster over the cover's items, proportional to their recalculated values.

  • Check that the regional and global cover totals match the balanced targets (toolExpectLessDiff, 10^-5).

Output properties: Ideally, the bioh of each cover stays parallel to the input after the harmonization year, regionally and globally, and so does the sum over both covers. When this is not possible, parallelism breaks as follows:

  1. A negative regional target is set to zero and the targets > 0 of the other regions are scaled down. The global cover total stays parallel, the parallelism of that region is lost.

  2. A cover whose global target is negative is set to zero, and the clipped loss is compensated for by the other cover. The global total of the cover set to zero is no longer parallel, the sum over both covers is.

  3. If a region has zero recalculated bioh, but target > 0, that bioh is moved to clusters in other regions (toolAllocateRegionTotals). If there is not enough capacity left, regional and global cover parallelism breaks, flagged by the tool's own checks as notes (no error).

Always true: a cluster never gets more than its recalculated bioh. The one exception is a region whose target exceeds its total recalculated bioh: there, every cluster gets its proportional share of the target, even if it exceeds its own recalculated bioh. Clusters with zero recalculated bioh never get anything.
